text:
Archinect is looking to expand our network of freelance writers and contributors for upcoming editorial projects.
We’re interested in hearing from writers with a strong understanding of architecture, design, practice, education, and the broader forces shaping the profession. Strong writing is essential, but we’re equally interested in people who think critically and insightfully about architecture and how the field is evolving.
Assignments will vary. Some pieces will originate from Archinect’s editorial team, while others may involve interviews, research, profiles, features, or editorial projects developed in collaboration with Archinect’s institutional partners. Topics may range from architectural practice and education to employment, technology, AI, culture, and emerging issues across the profession.
We’re particularly interested in writers who can bring more to an assignment than simply reporting the facts, people who can identify the larger questions behind a story, conduct thoughtful interviews, and develop a clear point of view or editorial framework while working within Archinect’s editorial standards.
This is freelance work on a per-assignment basis, but our goal is to develop longer-term relationships with writers whose interests and approach are a strong fit for Archinect.
What we're looking for
Excellent writing, reporting, and interviewing skills
A strong knowledge of architecture and the built environment
Curiosity about how architectural practice and culture are changing
The ability to develop an insightful angle rather than simply summarize a subject
Comfort working independently with interview subjects and source material
Reliability with deadlines and communication
Professional or academic experience in architecture, journalism, criticism, design, or related fields is welcome, but we are open to writers from a range of backgrounds
If you're interested, please send us a short introduction, a few examples of your writing, and a brief description of the subjects within architecture and design that you are most interested in exploring.
We'd also be interested in hearing about story ideas or areas of coverage you believe deserve more attention.
Archinect has been publishing independent architecture news, features, criticism, and professional resources since 1997, with an international audience of architects, designers, students, educators, and others working across the built environment.
